info.title: StreamLib runtime control API
info.description: Every operation a StreamLib runtime's control plane serves. `x-contract-version` is bumped only by a breaking change; an addition is marked by its method's `x-since`.

methods.name: discover
methods.summary: Answer the contract version this runtime serves, its version and build id, and every method it serves.
methods.description: Answer `contract_version`, the version of the contract this runtime serves, its `runtime_version` and `build_id`, and `operations`, every method it serves. A client sends the `contract_version` it was built against; another version is refused naming both, and the client is not served.

methods.name: subscribe_project_changes
methods.summary: Send this connection a `project_changed` notification for each change on the named projects' feeds.
methods.description: Subscribe the connection to the change feeds of `projects`, by UUID: from then on, each transaction applied to one, each action the runtime refuses on one and each media facts read it finishes is sent as a `project_changed` notification, whoever made it, until the connection closes. Served only on a connection that stays open; refused for an empty `projects`. Answers every project the connection is subscribed to.

methods.name: describe_runtime
methods.summary: Describe this runtime: its version, its build id, how long it has been up and where it logs.
methods.description: Describe this runtime: its crate `version`, its `build_id` (`<version>+<git sha>.<per-build nonce>`, telling two builds of one version apart), `up_for_ms`, the monotonic milliseconds since its engine started — a restart resets it — and `runtime_log_directory`, the folder its own log is written to, `null` when it keeps none. Names no stream.

methods.name: list_streams
methods.summary: List every stream the runtime holds, by stream id, with its location and state.
methods.description: List every stream the runtime holds: its stream id as `stream`, its `display_name`, its `location` — its project directory, its project's UUID as `project` and its stream asset's UUID as `stream_asset`, `null` for a record an earlier runtime wrote — and its state: `running` (playing, or recorded playing and re-loaded playing at the runtime's next start), `stopped` (open with its playback stopped, its graph loaded to read and edit while its node count is set, until `start_playback`), `paused` (open with its playback paused by `pause_playback`, until `resume_playback`), `closed` (its project closed by `close_project`, not loaded, until `open_project`), `preparing` (an action that loads it — an `open_project`, `reload_project` or `start_playback` — is queued or under way on it, named by `action`, on its `step`: `reading_the_graph_documents`, `making_the_venv` or `starting`, `null` while it waits), `stopping` (a `stop_playback`, `close_project` or `remove_project` of its project is queued or under way on it, named by `action`, on the step `stopping`, `null` while it waits), or `failed` (its code, its venv, its load or its start failed, and held stopped from its document when that reads, its graph there to read and edit, until a play or a `reload_project` retries it; implicated in the runtime's last two crashes in a row, and held at a start from its document with none of its node code read until a `reload_project` of its project tries it; or recorded by an earlier runtime, never loaded, with `failed_because` saying to run it again and `remove_project` forgetting it), with the node count of its loaded graph (`null` when it is not loaded), `failed_because`, why a failed stream failed (`null` otherwise), and `capture_devices_whose_access_was_never_asked_for`, each of `camera` and `microphone` that a node of the loaded stream refused because nobody has asked the user for its access, as when the runtime re-loaded the stream on its own at its start (empty otherwise): a `close_project` then `open_project` of its project asks.

methods.name: graph
methods.summary: Export a loaded stream's live graph, or every loaded stream's, with each node's and link's state.
methods.description: Export a loaded stream's current graph as JSON: the stream it was loaded as, its nodes by name with their types, config and ports, its links by node and port, with each node's and link's live state and counters beside them, and this machine's name (`machine`), the first part of `<machine>/<stream id>/<node>/<port>`. A fragment — a graph generator's stored output — renders as one node of `kind` `fragment` whose ports are its Graph Input and Output nodes' and whose `fragment` holds its own nodes and links, a fragment inside it rendered the same way; its nodes run under their path of names, `look/soft/blur`. Without `stream`, `{machine, streams}` holds every loaded stream's graph.

methods.name: transact
methods.summary: Apply operations on one project's stream graphs as one transaction, whole or not at all.
methods.description: Apply operations on the graphs of one project's loaded streams as one transaction by its `author`: applied in order, whole or not at all, to each running stream, and with `mode` `commit`, the default, written to each stream's graph document and recorded as one commit on the project's history, which `undo` reverses as one. Answers `mode`, the `transaction` and `commit` recording a committed edit, each operation as applied, `added_nodes` with each new node's UUID and the name it took, and `connected_links` with each new link's `state` — `pending`, `wired`, or `error` with its `error_reason`. Refused whole, in the runtime's own words, with nothing changed. A config value `{"asset": "<uuid>"}` must name an asset the project holds. An `add_node` may give its node an `as`, which later operations of the same transaction name the node by. The transaction is announced on the project's change feed, the resource `list_assets` names as `transactions_resource_uri`.

methods.name: add_node
methods.summary: Add a node to a loaded stream's graph by its type's import path, as one transaction.
methods.description: Add a node to a loaded stream's graph by its type's import path, as one transaction, the runtime making the node's UUID. A Python type is named `module:QualifiedClassName` and must be importable by the stream's own interpreter — a module in the stream's project, or a package installed in its venv: the runtime never imports it, and describes it in that interpreter the first time it is added; each add spawns it in its own processor interpreter, which imports the module fresh. The type's port declaration is read when it is first described and kept; to change a type's ports, add it under a new class name.

methods.name: connect
methods.summary: Link an output port to an input port in one loaded stream, as one transaction.
methods.description: Link an output port to an input port in one loaded stream, as one transaction, each end a node's UUID and a port name `graph` lists under that node's `ports`. A stream reads another stream's track at a relay through a `MoqTrackReceive` node. A link is spliced in by connecting a new node on both sides, then disconnecting the link it replaces — or all three in one `transact`.

methods.name: import_graph_generator
methods.summary: Run one of the project's `@graph_generator` functions in the stream's own interpreter and place what it builds in a loaded stream's graph as a fragment node, as one transaction.
methods.description: Run one of the project's `@graph_generator` functions in the stream's own interpreter and place what it builds in a loaded stream's graph as a fragment node, as one transaction: its generator as `type`, its promoted settings as `config`, and the nodes and links it built stored under `fragment`, each node with a UUID of its own. Run again under the name of a fragment the graph holds, it refreshes that fragment with the fresh run: each node it builds keeps the UUID of the node of the same name it built before, so links into the fragment and the graph's history hold. A generator that raises, refuses, or is not found is refused with its traceback, nothing changed. Answers as `transact` does, a new fragment node under `added_nodes`; undo restores the fragment as it was.

methods.name: remove_node
methods.summary: Remove a node from a loaded stream's graph by its UUID, as one transaction, stopping it.
methods.description: Remove a node from a loaded stream's graph by its UUID, as one transaction, stopping it; its links go with it, and undo brings both back.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.summary: Take out the link between an output port and an input port in one loaded stream, as one transaction, each end a node's UUID and a port name.
methods.description: Take out the link between an output port and an input port in one loaded stream, as one transaction, each end a node's UUID and a port name.

methods.name: set_node_config
methods.summary: Replace a node's config whole, as one transaction, applied to the running node at the stream's next commit.
methods.description: Replace a node's config whole, as one transaction, applied to the running node at the stream's next commit. A config value `{"asset": "<uuid>"}` references an asset of the project, which then cannot be deleted while the reference stands.

methods.name: set_pin_value
methods.summary: Set the value one of a node's inputs holds while no link feeds it, as one transaction.
methods.description: Set the value one of a node's inputs holds while no link feeds it, as one transaction; the value is saved in the graph document as a link is.

methods.name: rename_node
methods.summary: Give a node another name, a label, as one transaction.
methods.description: Give a node another name, a label, as one transaction; the node keeps its UUID, which every address names it by. Refused while another node's config names it by its name.

methods.name: set_studio_fields
methods.summary: Replace what Tato Studio draws a node with — canvas position, group, comment, colour, collapsed, and a client's own `metadata` — as one transaction, the old fields replaced whole.
methods.description: Replace what Tato Studio draws a node with — canvas position, group, comment, colour, collapsed, and a client's own `metadata` — as one transaction, the old fields replaced whole. The fields are held to the studio contract: a key of the wrong shape, or any key outside it, is refused by name. It changes nothing that runs.

methods.name: set_exposed_config_fields
methods.summary: Replace the config fields a node takes as inputs, as one transaction.
methods.description: Replace the config fields a node takes as inputs, as one transaction. Each is a number or bool field of the node's config schema and becomes an input of the field's name: linked, it drives the field, a function node reading it at each evaluation and a process node taking each new value as a live config update; unlinked, it reads the node's config. A field still linked cannot be taken off.

methods.name: add_group
methods.summary: Make a labelled group of nodes of one level of a loaded stream, its own or the subgraph `level` names, as one transaction.
methods.description: Make a labelled group of nodes of one level of a loaded stream, its own or the subgraph `level` names, as one transaction: a title, a description and a colour Tato Studio frames the nodes with, so the next reader knows what they do. It changes nothing that runs. Each node joins it by holding the group's UUID as its `studio.group`; a node of another group is refused, and a node leaves or joins later through `set_studio_fields`. Answers as `transact` does, the new group's UUID under `added_groups`.

methods.name: set_group_fields
methods.summary: Set a labelled group's title, description or colour, as one transaction.
methods.description: Set a labelled group's title, description or colour, as one transaction; a field omitted is kept. Its nodes stay as they are.

methods.name: collapse_selection_into_subgraph
methods.summary: Collapse nodes of one level of a loaded stream, its own or the subgraph `level` names, into one subgraph node, as one transaction.
methods.description: Collapse nodes of one level of a loaded stream, its own or the subgraph `level` names, into one subgraph node, as one transaction with `mode` `commit`: the nodes and the links between them are saved as a new stream of the project, `streams/<name>.graph.json`, and placed by reference where they were, so editing inside the subgraph edits that stream everywhere it is placed, and it runs only where it is placed. Each link that crossed the selection is carried through a `GraphInput` or `GraphOutput` of the new stream, named `<node>-<port>` and of the family the running stream declares at the link's source, so the stream runs the same nodes, each under the subgraph's name (`sub/blur`) and the UUID its placement gives it. Answers as `transact` does, the subgraph node under `added_nodes`; undo gives back the exact earlier graph document and takes the new stream out again, refused while another stream places it.

methods.name: unlock_subgraph
methods.summary: Unlock a subgraph node of one level of a loaded stream, its own or the subgraph `level` names, as one transaction.
methods.description: Unlock a subgraph node of one level of a loaded stream, its own or the subgraph `level` names, as one transaction: its nodes and the links between them become plain nodes of its level, its `GraphInput` and `GraphOutput` nodes go, and each link into or out of one of its ports is carried straight to the node it fed or read. A graph generator's output unlocked this way is no longer refreshed. A placed stream's nodes come back as a copy under new UUIDs that no edit of that stream then reaches, and the stream stays in the project, running as its own stream once nothing places it. Refused for a node of the subgraph named as a node of the level is; undo gives back the exact earlier graph document.

methods.name: add_note
methods.summary: Place a canvas note on a loaded stream's graph, as one transaction.
methods.description: Place a canvas note on a loaded stream's graph, as one transaction: text at a position and size Tato Studio draws it at, beside the nodes rather than on one. It changes nothing that runs. Answers as `transact` does, the new note's UUID under `added_notes`.

methods.name: set_note_fields
methods.summary: Set a canvas note's text, position or size, as one transaction.
methods.description: Set a canvas note's text, position or size, as one transaction; a field omitted is kept.

methods.name: remove_note
methods.summary: Take a canvas note off a loaded stream's graph, as one transaction.
methods.description: Take a canvas note off a loaded stream's graph, as one transaction. Undo puts it back as it was.

methods.name: remove_group
methods.summary: Take out a labelled group, as one transaction.
methods.description: Take out a labelled group, as one transaction: its nodes stay, ungrouped. Undo brings the group back with every node that belonged to it.

methods.name: open_project
methods.summary: Queue the open of a project: its streams are loaded and held with their playback stopped.
methods.description: Open the project in `project_directory`: queue its open on its own stream action queue and answer at once with the action's id as `action`. The open reads its `tatolab-project.json` and each stream asset's graph document, makes the project's `.venv` with the uv the runtime carries when its `.venv/bin/python` does not run — however long uv takes — then loads each stream under its stream id, `<project>-<stream>-<hash>`, the hash over the project's UUID and the stream asset's UUID, and holds it with its playback stopped, recording each stream stopped or failed: a graph document that does not load, or a load that is refused, with its reason, and a `.venv` uv cannot make — uv's own words — failing every stream of the project. It starts no node. Once it is done, `graph`, every graph edit and the node catalog answer for each stream, and `start_playback` plays the project. The project stays open, held stopped or playing, across the runtime's restarts until `close_project`. It opens a project that was never opened, one `close_project` closed, and one whose every stream failed, retrying them. One project's actions run one at a time, in the order they were queued; different projects' run side by side. Follow the action with `describe_stream_action`, its streams with `list_streams` — `preparing`, with the action and its `step`, until it ends — and its records with `logs` given `action`. A directory that does not exist or holds no `tatolab-project.json` fails the action, never the call. Refused, with nothing queued: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, and a project open once its queued actions run, which `reload_project` refreshes.

methods.name: reload_project
methods.summary: Queue a soft reload of an open project from disk, keeping its playback.
methods.description: Softly reload the open project in `project_directory` from disk: queue the load on its stream action queue and answer at once with the action's id as `action`. It re-reads every stream asset's graph document. While the project's node code — its `.py` files, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and views' `tatolab_view.json` — is as it was at a stream's load, the stream stays loaded and its graph is brought to its document in place, each node matched by its UUID, so only the nodes and links that changed change; otherwise the stream is loaded again under its same id, keeping its display name. A stream whose graph document is gone is unloaded and forgotten, a failed stream is loaded again, and the project's `.venv` is synced only when its dependency files changed or its `.venv/bin/python` does not run. The project keeps its playback: a playing project's streams start playing, a paused one's start paused, and a stopped one's are held stopped. `tatolab dev` asks for it on each save. A hard reload is `close_project` then `open_project`. Follow it as `open_project`'s open. Refused, with nothing queued: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, and a project that is not open, which `open_project` opens.

methods.name: close_project
methods.summary: Queue the close of an open project: its streams are unloaded and stay closed until it is opened.
methods.description: Close the open project in `project_directory`: queue the close on its stream action queue and answer at once with the action's id as `action`. Once the project's earlier actions have run, it ends the playback of every stream of the project, unloads each, forgets its function-node state, and records each closed, so the runtime leaves the project unloaded across its restarts until `open_project` opens it again. It deletes nothing: the project's files, its `.venv` and what uv synced into it stay. Its streams are `stopping` in `list_streams` until it ends, then `closed`; follow it with `describe_stream_action`. Each recorded stream carries the close on its record until it has run, so a runtime crash finishes it at the next start. Refused, with nothing queued: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, and a project that is not open once its queued actions run.

methods.name: remove_project
methods.summary: Queue the removal of a project from the runtime: its streams are stopped and their records forgotten.
methods.description: Queue the removal of the whole project in `project_directory` on its stream action queue and answer at once with the action's id as `action`: once the project's earlier actions have run, it unloads every loaded stream of the project and forgets every record of it, so the runtime no longer re-loads any of them, and deletes no file. `delete_asset` on a stream asset unloads and forgets that one stream. The project's streams are `stopping` in `list_streams` until it ends; follow it with `describe_stream_action`. Refused, with nothing queued: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, and a project the runtime holds no stream of.

methods.name: start_playback
methods.summary: Queue the start of an open project's playback.
methods.description: Start the playback of the open project in `project_directory`: queue it on the project's stream action queue and answer at once with the action's id as `action`. Once the project's earlier actions have run, each stream the project holds stopped starts fresh from the graph it holds, edits made while stopped included, reading no graph document and making no `.venv`: every node instance is made anew, so only the state a node persists itself carries over from an earlier playback. Each stream is recorded running, so the runtime plays the project again across its restarts until `stop_playback`. A project plays or stops as a whole: no tool plays or stops one of its streams. Follow it with `describe_stream_action`. Refused, with nothing queued: a `project_directory` that is not absolute; a project that is not open, which `open_project` opens; a paused project, which `resume_playback` resumes; and a project that plays once its queued actions run, which `stop_playback` stops.

methods.name: stop_playback
methods.summary: Queue the stop of a project's playback, its streams staying loaded.
methods.description: Stop the playback of the whole project in `project_directory`: queue the stop on its stream action queue and answer at once with the action's id as `action` beside the `project_directory`. Once the project's earlier actions have run, it ends the playback of every loaded stream of the project — every processor instance, device claim, function-node state and the clock torn down — keeps each stream's graph loaded, so `graph`, every graph edit and the node catalog still answer for it, and records each stopped, so the runtime holds the project open and stopped across its restarts until `start_playback` plays it again from the graph it holds. Its streams are `stopping` in `list_streams` until it ends; follow it with `describe_stream_action`. Each recorded stream carries the stop on its record until it has run, so a runtime crash finishes it at the next start. Refused, with nothing queued: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, a project whose removal is queued, and a project none of whose streams plays once the actions queued before it run.

methods.name: pause_playback
methods.summary: Pause a playing project's playback at once.
methods.description: Pause the playback of the whole project in `project_directory` at once, never waiting behind an action on its queue, and answer the `project_directory` and, as `streams`, the id of each loaded stream this call paused. Every processor of each loaded stream holds its state and processes nothing, and a scaled or stepped stream clock holds where it stands, opening no step, while a real-time clock is the machine's own and runs on; the streams stay loaded and are `paused` in `list_streams`, and a graph edit made meanwhile is applied and compiles on `resume_playback`. The project stays paused until `resume_playback`, `stop_playback`, `close_project` or `remove_project`: a stream a `reload_project` loads meanwhile, the one `tatolab dev` asks for on a save among them, starts paused. Pause is recorded, so a runtime restart re-loads the project paused. Pausing a paused project pauses nothing more. Refused: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, and a project none of whose streams plays — none loaded, or each held stopped, which `start_playback` plays — and whose last action queued is not a `start_playback`.

methods.name: resume_playback
methods.summary: Resume a paused project's playback at once.
methods.description: Resume the paused playback of the project in `project_directory` at once and answer the `project_directory` and, as `streams`, the id of each stream this call resumed: every processor carries on from the state it held, each held stream clock carries on from the stream time it was held at, and each stream compiles the graph edits made while it was paused, a compile that fails logged in the project's `logs` as a live edit's is. Refused: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, and a project that is not paused.

methods.name: describe_stream_action
methods.summary: Describe one stream action by its id: its state, its step and each stream it reached.
methods.description: Describe the stream action `action`: its project, `kind` (`open`, `load`, `start_playback`, `stop`, `close`, `remove`, `delete` or `reload_at_start`), `state` — `queued` behind the project's earlier actions, `in_progress` on its `step` (`reading_the_graph_documents`, `making_the_venv`, `starting`), `done`, `failed` with `failed_because`, or `cancelled` by `cancel_stream_action` — its `venv_sync`, what its latest uv sync of the project's `.venv` has done, read from uv's own lines from the moment uv starts and kept once it ends, `null` for an action that has not synced: its `phase` (`resolving`, `downloading`, `building`, `installing`, `installed`), `packages_resolved`, `packages_prepared` and `packages_installed` as uv counts them, `downloads_started` and `downloads_done` of the downloads uv names — only those over about a MiB — and under `packages` each package uv named, first named first, by `name`, `version` once uv names it, `kind` (`distribution` or `python_interpreter`), `state` (`downloading`, `downloaded`, `building`, `built`, `installed`, `uninstalled`) and `download_size_bytes` as uv states it; uv names no byte of a download as it arrives — and `streams`, each stream its project's graph documents named by `stream` id and `display_name`, with its `state` `running`, `stopped` or `failed` once the action took it in. Followed live as the resource `streamlib://stream-action/<action>`, which a `subscriptions/listen` naming it is sent `notifications/resources/updated` for each time the action changes. The runtime holds every queued and running action and the last 64 finished ones of each project; an older one is refused, its records still in the project's `logs`.

methods.name: cancel_stream_action
methods.summary: Cancel one stream action that is still queued or under way.
methods.description: Cancel the stream action `action`, the only way an action ends early; nothing replaces or edits a queued one. A queued action is dropped from its project's queue, its pending mark taken off each stream's record so the record stays as it was, and answers `cancelled`. A running `open`, `load` or `reload_at_start` answers `in_progress` and stops at the step it is on — a running uv sync is killed and a half-made `.venv` removed — then ends `cancelled`: a stream it was loading is recorded failed, and the streams it had not reached stay as recorded. Refused for a running `stop`, `close` or `remove`, whose unload has begun and cannot be cut short, which ends `done`; for an action already finished; and for one the runtime does not hold.

methods.name: rename_project
methods.summary: Rename a project, as one transaction on its history.
methods.description: Rename a project, as one transaction by `author` on its history that undoes like any edit: its `name` in `tatolab-project.json` changes, and its UUID, its folder and its streams' ids stay as they are. Answers how people see the project now, with the `transaction` and `commit`. Refused for a blank name.

methods.name: set_project_description
methods.summary: Describe a project, or clear its description, as one transaction on its history.
methods.description: Describe a project, or clear its description, as one transaction by `author` on its history that undoes like any edit: its `description` in `tatolab-project.json`, served by `list_assets` as `project_description`. Answers how people see the project now, with the `transaction` and `commit`.

methods.name: set_project_cover
methods.summary: Give a project a cover, or take it away, as one transaction on its history.
methods.description: Give a project a cover, or take it away, as one transaction by `author` on its history that undoes like any edit: its `cover` in `tatolab-project.json` names a media asset the project holds by its UUID, served by `list_assets` as `project_cover`. An image a person picks, or a frame a viewer showed, is first imported with `import_asset` and then named here; the asset cannot be deleted while it is the cover. Answers how people see the project now, with the `transaction` and `commit`. Refused for an asset the project does not hold, or one that is not a media asset.

methods.name: duplicate_project
methods.summary: Duplicate a project into a folder that does not exist yet, as a project of its own.
methods.description: Duplicate a project into `into`, a folder that does not exist yet, as a project of its own: every file a copy of it carries, its `imports/` included, and its whole history, so its edits can still be undone in the copy, under a new project UUID and the name `<name> copy`, the duplicate recorded as a commit on its history by `author`. Its `.venv` and the rest of its `.tatolab/` stay behind, and the duplicate is not opened: `open_project` opens it. Answers the duplicate's `project_directory`, `project`, `project_name` and `commit`. Refused, nothing left at `into`, for a relative `into`, one that exists, and one inside the project.

methods.name: delete_project
methods.summary: Queue the deletion of a whole project.
methods.description: Delete the whole project in `project_directory`: queue its deletion on its stream action queue and answer at once with the action's id as `action` beside the `project_directory`. Once the project's earlier actions have run, it unloads every loaded stream of the project and forgets every record of it, as `remove_project` does, then moves the project's folder to this machine's Trash, from which its owner can put it back. Its streams are `stopping` in `list_streams` until it ends; follow it with `describe_stream_action`, which answers `failed` with why when the folder could not be moved. Refused, with nothing queued: a `project_directory` that is not absolute, and a folder holding no `tatolab-project.json`.

methods.name: list_assets
methods.summary: List a project's assets, ordered by path.
methods.description: List a project's assets, ordered by path: each by its `asset` UUID, its `kind` (`stream`, `media`, `scene` or `data`), its `path` in the project, the SHA-256 and size of its bytes, its `import_settings`, and what the runtime has read from its bytes — `media_facts_state` (`read`, `reading`, `unreadable` with `media_facts_unreadable_because`, or `null` for a stream), `media_facts` and `preview`, as `describe_asset` answers them, each from what is already read, an asset not yet read queued for a read — with the project's UUID, `project_name`, `project_description`, `project_cover` — the UUID of the image asset it is shown by — and `project_last_edited_at`, when its history last changed in seconds since the Unix epoch, each `null` when it has none, and `transactions_resource_uri`, its change feed. `kind` narrows to one kind. Refused for a folder with no `tatolab-project.json`.

methods.name: describe_asset
methods.summary: Describe one asset of a project.
methods.description: Describe one asset of a project: its UUID, kind, path, the SHA-256 and size of its bytes, its import settings, `file_at_its_path`, whether a file is at its path, and what the runtime has read from its bytes, which it reads once per SHA-256 after an import or a replace and keeps in the project's `.tatolab/`. `media_facts_state` is `read`, `reading` — a read queued or under way, after which the project's change feed carries a `media_facts_read` entry — `unreadable`, with why in `media_facts_unreadable_because`, or `null` for a stream asset. `media_facts` carries `duration_ms`; `video` with `pixel_width`, `pixel_height`, `frames_per_second` and `codec`; `audio` with `sample_rate_hz`, `channel_count` and `codec`; `image` with `pixel_width` and `pixel_height`; `lut` with `lut_1d_size` or `lut_3d_size`, `domain_min` and `domain_max`; and `scene` — each `null` when the file does not hold or state it. `preview` is the size and `media_type` of the picture `read_asset_preview` answers, `null` when the asset has none.

methods.name: read_asset_preview
methods.summary: Read an asset's preview picture.
methods.description: Read an asset's preview picture, which the runtime makes from its bytes and keeps in the project's `.tatolab/`: a PNG at most 512 pixels on its longest edge, answered as `content_base64`, standard base64 with padding, with its `media_type`, `pixel_width`, `pixel_height` and `byte_len`. An image has one; video, audio, a LUT, a scene and other data have none yet, as `describe_asset`'s `preview` being `null` says. Refused while the runtime is still reading the asset's bytes — `describe_asset`'s `media_facts_state` reads `reading`, and the project's change feed carries a `media_facts_read` entry once it is done — for an asset with no preview, and for a stream asset.

methods.name: import_asset
methods.summary: Import a file as a new asset of a project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Import a file as a new asset of the project at `asset_path`, or, with no `asset_path`, in its kind's folder of the project's standard layout — `media/` for video, audio and images, `scenes/` for USD, glTF and other 3D scenes, `data/` for everything else — under `file_name` or the source file's own name, numbered `<name>-2.<extension>`, `-3`, … past a name an asset or another file already takes there. Answers the `asset`, with the UUID the runtime made for it, which every later relocation keeps, and the `path` it landed at, and the `transaction` and `commit` that record it. The bytes are copied once, to `asset_path`, and only the asset's sidecar, `<asset_path>.asset.json`, enters history. `source` is a file on this machine by absolute path, copied there, or an upload in the project's `.tatolab/uploads/` by its SHA-256, moved there; a file already at `asset_path` is imported in place. Undoing the import removes the file at `asset_path`, one imported in place included, and nothing keeps its bytes. Refused whole, with nothing written, for a path another asset or another file holds, a path outside the project, and a stream, which is never imported.

methods.name: relocate_asset
methods.summary: Move or rename an asset inside its project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Put an asset at another path of the project, renaming it, moving it to another folder or both, its sidecar going with it, as one transaction; the asset keeps its UUID. Answers the asset as it now is, with the `transaction` and `commit`.

methods.name: delete_asset
methods.summary: Delete an asset from a project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Stop tracking an asset as one transaction: its file and sidecar leave the project, and nothing keeps its bytes, so undoing the transaction brings back its sidecar and the asset reads missing until its file is at its path again. A stream asset's graph document leaves the project, recorded in the transaction so an undo writes it back, and its stream is unloaded and forgotten. Refused while a stream's graph document references the asset, the refusal naming each document. Answers the asset as it was, with the `transaction` and `commit`.

methods.name: set_asset_settings
methods.summary: Replace an asset's import settings, as one transaction.
methods.description: Replace an asset's import settings whole, as one transaction. Answers the asset as it now is, with the `transaction` and `commit`.

methods.name: replace_asset
methods.summary: Replace an asset's bytes, as one transaction.
methods.description: Put new bytes at an asset's path as one transaction: the asset keeps its UUID, path, kind and settings, so every node referencing it reads the new bytes at its next load, and its sidecar records their SHA-256 and size. `source` is a file on this machine by absolute path, copied there, or an upload in the project's `.tatolab/uploads/` by its SHA-256, moved there. The bytes replaced are kept as an upload under their SHA-256, so an undo puts them back with the earlier sidecar; history records the sidecar alone. A file replaced outside the runtime is not supported. Answers the asset as it now is, with the `transaction` and `commit`; bytes the sidecar already records apply nothing and are refused as an empty transaction. Refused for a stream asset, whose graph document graph edits change.

methods.name: create_stream
methods.summary: Create a stream in a project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Create a stream in the project as one transaction: a new stream asset, its graph document written at `path` holding no nodes, its UUID, which the runtime makes, and its `display_name`. While the project runs, the new stream is loaded on the project's queue and the answer carries that load's `action`, which `describe_stream_action` follows. Answers the stream asset as `asset`, with the `transaction` and `commit`; an undo takes the document out and unloads the stream. Refused for a path another file holds or outside the project, and a blank `display_name`.

methods.name: delete_stream
methods.summary: Delete a stream from a project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Delete a stream from the project as one transaction: its graph document leaves the project, recorded in the transaction so an undo writes it back and loads the stream again while the project runs, and its stream is unloaded and forgotten. Answers the stream asset as it was, with the `transaction` and `commit`. Refused for a UUID the project holds no stream asset under.

methods.name: set_stream_display_name
methods.summary: Set the name a stream is shown under, as one transaction.
methods.description: Show a stream under another display name as one transaction, written in its graph document so every machine the project is on shows it and an undo writes the earlier one. A loaded stream is shown under it at once and keeps its stream id. Answers the stream asset as it now is, with the `transaction` and `commit`. Refused for a blank `display_name`.

methods.name: add_dependency
methods.summary: Import another project into a project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Import another project, as one transaction by `author`: the project `source` holds, a folder or a `.zip` of one on this machine, is copied whole into `imports/<folder>/` and recorded in `tatolab-project.json` under `dependencies` with the `version` its copy carries, the SHA-256 over its files. Nothing reaches the network. The copy is this project's own from then on: its assets are referenced as `{"asset": "<uuid>", "from": "<project uuid>"}` and read from its folder, its streams are placed with `use_dependency_stream`, and to edit it, open `imports/<folder>/` as a project of its own. Answers the `dependency`. Refused, nothing copied, for a source holding no `tatolab-project.json` or no project UUID in it, naming what is missing, for this project itself, a project already imported, or a folder already held.

methods.name: update_dependency
methods.summary: Bring an imported project up to date with its source, as one transaction.
methods.description: Copy an import again, whole, as one transaction by `author`, from `source` or from the source it was last copied from, replacing its folder under `imports/` and its `version`. Every loaded stream holding one of its streams as a fragment follows the new copy. When files of its folder were edited since its copy, nothing changes: it answers them under `edited_files` with `overwrite_confirmation_needed`, and is sent again with `overwrite_edited_files` to overwrite them. Undo puts the folder back as it was. Refused, nothing changed, for a project not imported, or a source holding another project.

methods.name: list_dependencies
methods.summary: List the projects a project imports.
methods.description: List the projects this one imports, each with its `folder`, `source` and `version` as `tatolab-project.json` holds them, and the files of its folder edited since its copy under `edited_files`; changes nothing. With `check_for_newer`, each source is read again and each import also answers `version_on_the_source` and `newer_version_exists`, or, for a source that could not be read, `check_refused_because`; nothing is copied until `update_dependency` copies it.

methods.name: remove_dependency
methods.summary: Take an imported project out of a project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Stop importing a project, as one transaction by `author`: its folder leaves `imports/` and its entry `tatolab-project.json`; undo puts both back as they were. Answers the `dependency` as it was. Refused, nothing changed, while a node of any of this project's streams — a fragment holding one of its streams, or a config holding `{"asset", "from"}` naming it, at any depth — still references it, naming each such node. Refused for a project not imported.

methods.name: use_dependency_stream
methods.summary: Place an imported project's stream in a loaded stream's graph as a fragment node, as one transaction.
methods.description: Place a stream of an imported project in a loaded stream's graph, as one committed transaction: a fragment node of type `tatolab.project:StreamFragment` whose config `{"stream": {"asset", "from"}}` references the stream. The graph document stores the reference alone; each load, and each change to the stream or its import, places the stream's nodes and links as its graph document under `imports/<folder>/` is on disk, each node under the UUID UUIDv5(fragment node's UUID, its own). Its Graph Input and Output nodes are the fragment's ports. Answers as `transact` does. Refused for a name a node of the graph already holds, and for a stream that holds the stream it is placed in, naming each stream of the cycle.

methods.name: list_project_files
methods.summary: List the files of a project that are not assets.
methods.description: List the project's files, or those under `under`, each by its path and length in bytes, sorted by path. Hidden folders such as `.tatolab/`, Python virtual environments, `node_modules/`, `__pycache__/` and symbolic links are not listed.

methods.name: read_project_file
methods.summary: Read one file of a project.
methods.description: Read one of the project's files whole, answering its bytes as `content_base64`, standard base64 with padding, its `byte_len`, and its `content_sha256`, which a `write_project_file` sends back as `expected_sha256`. Refused for a path that is not a file of the project.

methods.name: create_node_file
methods.summary: Create a node file in a project from the template, as one transaction.
methods.description: Create a new node file of the project from the runtime's node template, as one transaction an undo reverses: a `@node.process` class in the current `tatolab.stream` idiom, named after the file, with one Image input `video_in` whose frames it hands on unchanged to one Image output `video_out`, each with its description. It loads as a node type of the project with no edits and `list_project_node_types` lists it at once. Answers the `path`, the `node_type` it declares — `<module>:<class>`, what `add_node` takes — and the `transaction` and `commit`. Refused for a path that already holds a file, that is not a `.py` file importable as a Python module, or whose class name the template cannot declare, and for every path `write_project_file` refuses.

methods.name: write_project_file
methods.summary: Write one file of a project, as one transaction.
methods.description: Write one of the project's files whole, as one transaction: a new file is created with its folders, an existing one overwritten. An undo puts back what the file held, or takes a new file out. Answers the `path`, the `content_sha256` of the bytes written, and the `transaction` and `commit`. With `expected_sha256`, refused when the file changed or was taken out since it was read, so a save never overwrites another change. Content the file already holds is refused, as it changes nothing. Refused for what another tool changes — a stream's graph document, an asset's sidecar or bytes (`replace_asset`), `tatolab-project.json`, a file under `imports/` — and for a file inside a hidden folder or a Python virtual environment, which history does not record.

methods.name: list_project_node_types
methods.summary: List the node types a project offers, from its own node files and the packages it installs.
methods.description: List the node types and graph generators a project offers, read from source without running any of its code: its own node code outside `imports/`, each import's as its folder holds it now, and each installed distribution that declares `tatolab.nodes` entry points, each under `sources` by `source` (`project`, `dependency` or `installed_distribution`). A node type has its `type` (what `add_node` takes; an import's is led by its folder, `imports/<folder>/<module>:<class>`, and imported from there), `kind` (`process`, `function` or `shader`), `description`, `category`, and `inputs` and `outputs` where its declaration states them, each port's `family` null where source alone does not say. A graph generator has its `generator` (what `import_graph_generator` takes), its docstring as `description`, and its `promoted_config`. A module that does not parse is listed under its source's `unreadable_modules` with why and where; the rest still lists.

methods.name: list_project_views
methods.summary: List the Tato Studio views a project brings.
methods.description: List every Tato Studio view a project brings — each folder of its own `views/`, then of each import's `imports/<folder>/views/` — read from the folder's `tatolab_view.json` without running anything in it. Each view under `views` has its `view_type`, `<project name>:<view folder>`, which is a node type of each stream the project runs when the view opens and its `placement` is `node`; the `project`, `project_name` and `import_folder` (null for the project's own) of the project bringing it; its `view_folder_in_the_project`, the folder relative to the project, as `views/<folder>` or `imports/<import>/views/<folder>`, which names its files to a project file read; its `title`, `description`, `icon`, `preview` and `placement` (`area` or `node`); its declared `inputs` and `outputs`, each a `name`, a `family`, a `description` and an Array port's `range`; and its `manifest` as written. A folder whose manifest is missing, is not JSON, or does not read against view contract 1.0 is listed with `opens` false and why in `not_opened_because`; the rest still lists.

methods.name: write_studio_view_output
methods.summary: Write a value a Tato Studio view produced onto its node's output port.
methods.description: Hand a value a Tato Studio panel wrote to the view node `node` of the stream `stream`, which publishes it on its output `port` to every link and viewer reading that port, stamped with stream time now. A view node is a node of a view type, `<project name>:<view folder>`, which each view of the stream's project or of one of its imports is when it opens and its `placement` is `node`; its ports are the view's declared inputs and outputs, and a panel reads its inputs with `open_viewer` on the port linked into each. A write is live data: the last value written is what a reader keeps, many panels may write one node and the last write wins, and nothing is recorded in the graph document or the project's history. Array, Channels and Records outputs are written; an Image or Packets output is refused. Refused for a stream whose project is stopped, naming `start_playback`; a node of another type; a node that is not running; and a value its port's family does not take. A refusal because the node does not run comes with `structuredContent.refusal.not_running_because` naming why: `playback_stopped`, `playback_paused` (a node added while its project is paused), `preparing` or `node_failed`, the runtime's words beside it in `runtime_words`.

methods.name: write_graph_input
methods.summary: Write a value onto one of a loaded stream's graph inputs.
methods.description: Hand a value to the Input `input` of the stream `stream`: the stream's top-level `GraphInput` declaring it publishes the value on its `value` output to every node it is linked to, stamped with stream time now, and each reads it on its next process. A write is live data: many clients may write one Input and the last write wins, and nothing is recorded in the graph document or the project's history. An Input whose config's `lifetime` is `kept`, the default, keeps the last value in the project's store, so it carries it again after a Stop, a reload and a restart of the runtime; a `reset` Input returns to its `default` at Stop. While the project is stopped, a `kept` Input takes the value into the store and carries it at the next Play, and `graph` shows it; a `reset` Input is refused as `playback_stopped`. Until a write, the Input carries its config's `default`, if it declares one. `graph` renders the value an Input carries now, or carries at the next Play while stopped, under its node's `graph_interface` component, as `current_value`. Array, Channels and Records Inputs are written; an Image or Packets Input runs nothing and is refused. Refused for an Input no top-level `GraphInput` declares, and a value its family does not take. A refusal because the Input's node does not run comes with `structuredContent.refusal.not_running_because` naming why: `playback_stopped`, `playback_paused` (a node added while its project is paused), `preparing` or `node_failed`, the runtime's words beside it in `runtime_words`.

methods.name: import_project
methods.summary: Import a project from an archive into a folder that does not exist yet.
methods.description: Make a new project in `project_directory` from the `.zip` of a project at `source`, as a Marketplace entry or a GitHub archive is handed over. Its files are unpacked as `add_dependency` copies a zip — every file its history would record and every asset, its `imports/` included, never a hidden folder such as its `.tatolab/`, a cache, a Python virtual environment or a symbolic link — under a new project UUID of its own, so the same zip imported twice makes two projects, and committed by `author` as the first commit of a history of its own. Nothing reaches the network and nothing runs: open it with `open_project`, and `start_playback` plays it. Answers the new `project_directory`, its `project` UUID, its `name` and the `commit`. Refused, nothing left behind, for a relative path, a `source` that is a folder or no zip archive, a zip holding no `tatolab-project.json` or no project UUID in it, naming what is missing, or a `project_directory` that already exists.

methods.name: logs
methods.summary: Read a project's log records after a cursor, oldest first.
methods.description: Read a project's log records after the cursor `after`, oldest first, each as the project's JSONL log on disk holds it: every stream of the project and every load of it writes that one log, each record stamped with its `stream` — none for a load's own lines, uv's among them — across the runtime's runs, whether the stream is still recorded or not. `stream` narrows to one stream's records, and `action` to the records of one stream action — every record its load wrote, uv's among them, and the records of the streams it started. Pass the result's `next_after` back as `after` to read on; `records_no_longer_held` is true when retention deleted the segment `after` named, so the page resumes at the oldest record held. A project that has logged nothing answers no records.

methods.name: open_viewer
methods.summary: Open a viewer of a node's output port, held open for the connection that opened it.
methods.description: Open a viewer of any output port of a running node, adding no node and changing no graph: the runtime holds the port's channel open and answers the `viewer` id, the `iceoryx2_domain_root` and the `channel` whose reserved subscriber slot the viewer takes from its own process. A viewer reads the latest message the node wrote and skips what it falls behind on, so it never slows the stream; an Image message names a pooled frame rather than carrying its pixels, and the viewer imports that frame's surface from the `surface_share_address` the way a helper process does. The viewer stays open until `close_viewer` or the end of the connection that opened it, so it is opened only over a connection that stays open: `/mcp/stdio` or `/control/ws`. Refused for a node that is not running, with `structuredContent.refusal.not_running_because` naming why: `playback_stopped`, `playback_paused` (a node added while its project is paused), `preparing` or `node_failed`, the runtime's words beside it in `runtime_words`.

methods.name: close_viewer
methods.summary: Close a viewer this connection opened.
methods.description: Close a viewer this connection opened, letting go of its port's channel.

methods.name: set_stream_clock_scale
methods.summary: Run a started stream's scaled clock at another scale from now on.
methods.description: Run a started stream's scaled clock at `scale` from now on: its stream time carries on from where it stands, never jumping or running backwards, and every node's `ctx.time`, write stamps and continuous pace follow the new scale. Above 1 the clock runs in steps of its `step_ns`, paced at the scale, behind the step barrier every node runs on; back at or under 1 it runs free again. Refused for a stream on the real or a stepped clock, and for a scale above 1 while the stream holds a node that paces itself (execution = manual) and is not paced by real time. Live only: the stream's next start runs the clock its graph document names.

methods.name: create_project
methods.summary: Queue the creation of a project from the starter or a sample.
methods.description: Create a project — the one `tatolab new` creates: the starter, its `tatolab-project.json`, one stream asset `streams/main.graph.json` holding the test pattern's one source, `pyproject.toml`, `.python-version` and `.gitignore`, or, given a `sample` that `list_samples` lists, a copy of that sample project under a new project UUID — committed as the first commit of the project's history, in `project_directory`, or with none in a folder `<adjective>-<noun>` drawn under `~/streams`, and queue its open, answering at once with the action's id as `action`, the stream id its `main` runs under as `stream`, and the resolved `project_directory`. The action writes the project's files, then opens it as `open_project` does — reads its graph documents, makes its `.venv`, however long uv takes, and holds its stream stopped until `start_playback` — the project named after its folder and its `main` stream shown under the folder's name. A directory already holding a file the create writes fails the action with nothing written. Follow it with `describe_stream_action` and `logs`; the project is recorded and re-loaded whenever the runtime starts, so a later session finds it in `list_streams`. Refused only for a `sample` the runtime unit does not carry, naming the ones it does, a relative `project_directory`, one that cannot be created, or, with none, a `HOME` that is unset or not absolute or a draw that finds no free folder.

methods.name: list_samples
methods.summary: List the sample projects a new project can be created from.
methods.description: List the sample projects the runtime unit carries at its own version, each by the `name` `create_project`'s `sample` takes, its `title` and a `summary` of what it shows, in name order: none for a runtime run outside a runtime unit.

methods.name: refresh_fragments
methods.summary: Refresh, as one transaction, every fragment whose graph generator a changed module defines.
methods.description: Refresh, as one transaction, every fragment of the project's loaded streams whose graph generator, or a generator nested in it, is defined in a module one of `changed_files` holds: each is run again with the promoted settings its fragment keeps, as `import_graph_generator` refreshes it, each node keeping its UUID by name. Answers as `transact` does; with no such fragment, it answers no operation and records no transaction. A generator that raises refuses the whole refresh with its traceback, nothing changed.

methods.name: undo
methods.summary: Undo an author's latest transaction in a project that is not undone yet, as a new transaction.
methods.description: Undo the latest transaction by `author` in the project that is not undone yet, applying its inverse as a new transaction: its graph edits to the running streams and their graph documents, its asset changes and file writes to the project. Only the author's own transactions are undone, so two authors' interleaved edits are each undone by their own author. An edit to a stream not loaded is applied to its graph document alone, and the stream of a stream document the undo takes out is unloaded and forgotten. Refused when the author has nothing left to undo, or when what it would undo no longer applies — a node another author removed since, or a stream document it would take out that was edited after it was written. Answers the transaction applied, with `undoes` naming the one it reversed.

methods.name: redo
methods.summary: Redo what an author's latest undo in a project reversed, as a new transaction.
methods.description: Redo what `author`'s latest undo in the project reversed, as a new transaction; a new edit by the author after the undo leaves nothing to redo. Answers the transaction applied, with `redoes` naming the one it reapplied.

x-notifications.name: project_changed
x-notifications.summary: A change on the feed of a project the connection subscribed to: a transaction applied, an action refused, or media facts read.

x-agent-discovery-tools.name: list_operation_groups
x-agent-discovery-tools.summary: List every operation the runtime serves, by group.
x-agent-discovery-tools.description: List every operation this runtime serves, by group, each with its name and one sentence saying what it does. The tools in this tool list are the ones used most; every other operation — a project's assets, files, dependencies, node types and views, each single graph edit, redo, viewers — is reached through `call_operation`. Start here when no listed tool does what you need, then read the operation's params with `describe_operations`.

x-agent-discovery-tools.name: describe_operations
x-agent-discovery-tools.summary: Describe operations: what each does, the params it takes and what it answers.
x-agent-discovery-tools.description: Describe operations by name, or every operation of one group: what each reads, changes and answers, the JSON Schema of its params and of its result, whether it only reads, and the contract version it arrived in. Call it before the first `call_operation` of an operation, and send the params exactly as its `params_schema` states them.

x-agent-discovery-tools.name: call_operation
x-agent-discovery-tools.summary: Call any operation the runtime serves, by name.
x-agent-discovery-tools.description: Call any operation `list_operation_groups` lists, by name, with its `params`. It answers exactly what the operation answers, and a refusal is the operation's own. An operation that is also a listed tool answers the same either way.

action.description: The action refused, by the name of the tool it was sent to.

refused_operation_index.description: The position, from 0, of the operation refused among those the action sent, when one was.

refused_node.description: The node the refused operation names, as the caller named it: a UUID or an `as` label.

refused_link.description: The link the refused operation names.

refused_field.description: The node's input or config field the refused operation names.

not_running_because.description: Why the node the action reached for does not run, when that is why it was refused.

runtime_words.description: Why, in the runtime's own words, never rewritten.

ProjectActionRefusalOnTheWire.description:
What a refused action answers under `refusal` in its tool result's `structuredContent`,
beside the same words as the result's text.

source.description: The output port the link carries from.

target.description: The input port the link carries into.

RefusedGraphLinkOnTheWire.description: The link a refused operation names, each end as the caller named it.

GraphLinkEndOnTheWire.description: One end of a link a graph tool names: a node by its UUID and one of its ports.

oneOf.description: Its project's playback is stopped.
Its project's playback is paused, and the node was added since.
Its stream is starting, or has not compiled the node yet.
The node failed.

NodeNotRunningBecauseOnTheWire.description: Why a node a refused action reached for does not run.

ControlContractVersionMismatch.description: The `data` of a `discover` refused for a client built against another contract version.

contract_version.description:
The contract version the client was built against; another version than the runtime's is
refused naming both.
The contract version this runtime serves.

build_id.description: The runtime's build id, `<version>+<git sha>.<per-build nonce>`.

operations.description: Every method this runtime serves, in registry order.

DiscoverResult.description: What `discover` answers: the contract a runtime serves and what it is.

projects.description: The projects, by UUID, whose changes the connection is sent; refused when empty.
Every project the connection is subscribed to, by UUID, this call's among them.

SubscribeProjectChangesResult.description: What `subscribe_project_changes` answers: the projects the connection is now sent changes of.

build_id.description: `<crate version>+<git sha>.<per-build nonce>`, the build the helper check compares.

up_for_ms.description: Monotonic milliseconds since this runtime's engine started; a restart resets it.

runtime_log_directory.description:
The folder the runtime's own log is written to, absolute for `tatolabd`; `None` when it
keeps none.

stream.description: The stream's id; every tool naming the stream takes it.

display_name.description: The label the stream is shown under.

location.description: Where the stream's code lives; `null` for a record an earlier runtime wrote.

state.description: Whether it is running, stopped or failed.

node_count.description: How many nodes its loaded graph holds; `null` when it is not loaded.

failed_because.description: Why it is failed; `null` when it is not.

capture_devices_whose_access_was_never_a.description:
Each capture device a node of the loaded stream refused because nobody has asked the user
for its access — the runtime re-loaded it on its own at its start — once each; a
`close_project` then `open_project` of its project asks. Empty when it is not loaded.

action.description:
